title: Gifts to the World: How to Hold Your Boundaries, and Everyone Else's
coreMove: Run the reciprocity check: protect your own limit, receive another person's no cleanly, and support crossed boundaries without making safety depend on you being bold.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers disappointed by a loved one's limit
exampleSpecs.stakes: A friend's no can be honored without guilt, sarcasm, or repeated negotiation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show cleanly receiving another person's no without making disappointment the other person's job.

exampleSpecs.audience: witnesses who need safe intervention choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: A witness can support a crossed boundary without making direct confrontation the only moral option.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Right To Be's bystander tools to pick a safe intervention path.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who overextend in public groups
exampleSpecs.stakes: One calm refusal can give a group permission to stop treating capacity as a loyalty test.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a visible limit changing what other people feel allowed to say.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse repair with access
exampleSpecs.stakes: A relative's limit can delay a needed talk without authorizing pressure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a person tolerating a no from family without turning repair into a demand.

exampleSpecs.audience: witnesses weighing safety, privacy, and intervention
exampleSpecs.stakes: Documenting can support a targeted person only when care, consent, and safety guide the record.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Right To Be's options without treating recording as a replacement for care.

exampleSpecs.audience: people setting norms in informal groups
exampleSpecs.stakes: A person can model limits by redirecting a group before someone is exposed.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show one person's group limit protecting another person's privacy.
